title: write-cache microbenchmarks
question: What does a write-cache hit and miss cost against PGlite?
conclusions: In Write Cache Cold Miss Performance, Cold miss rebuild (1000 operations) is 78.29x slower than Cold miss with keyframe optimization (100 ops, keyframe at 50)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit with multiple revisions in ring buffer is 1.14x slower than Cache hit (latest revision)
In Write Cache Warm Miss Performance, Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations) is 6.86x slower than Warm miss with nearby cached revision
In Write Cache LRU Eviction Performance, LRU eviction (filling cache to capacity) is 3.02x slower than LRU access pattern (updating access order)
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline, With cache: rebuild (1000 operations) is 62.33x slower than No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (100 operations)
In Write Cache Keyframe Performance, Keyframe persistence overhead (every 10th revision) is 1x slower than Without keyframe persistence (interval = 1000000)
caveats: The no-cache baseline compares a cold cache rebuild against a manual replay, and a cold rebuild is a replay, so that pair reads about 1x by construction rather than measuring what the cache is worth
The two keyframe cases are floored by a 100ms drain sleep that lets fire-and-forget keyframe writes land, so their difference is not a measure of persistence overhead

Write Cache Warm Miss Performance / Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations): 52 samples, too few for the spread to mean much

title: write-cache microbenchmarks with the cold-miss replay decomposed
question: what a cold-miss rebuild spends per operation, split into the draft, the reducer body, and the input validation inside it
conclusions: In Write Cache Cold Miss Performance, Cold miss rebuild (1000 operations) is 60.6x slower than Cold miss with keyframe optimization (100 ops, keyframe at 50)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit with multiple revisions in ring buffer is 1.12x slower than Cache hit (latest revision)
In Write Cache Warm Miss Performance, Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations) is 6.87x slower than Warm miss with nearby cached revision
In Write Cache LRU Eviction Performance, LRU eviction (filling cache to capacity) is 3.02x slower than LRU access pattern (updating access order)
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline, No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (1000 operations) is 72.74x slower than With cache: rebuild (100 operations)
In Write Cache Keyframe Performance, Keyframe persistence overhead (every 10th revision) is 1x slower than Without keyframe persistence (interval = 1000000)
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (100 ops), cold miss 100 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 3.38x slower than cold miss 100 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (500 ops), cold miss 500 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 7.99x slower than cold miss 500 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (1000 ops), cold miss 1000 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 13.5x slower than cold miss 1000 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (2000 ops), cold miss 2000 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 25.86x slower than cold miss 2000 ops: input validation only

Per-call zod schema construction is 34.89us of the 35.54us state-independent constant in the drive reducer body, or 98.2%: the input-validation-only leg is flat in op count at 34.88/35.11/35.15/35.50us/op for 100/500/1000/2000 ops, fitting 34.89us with a per-node slope of +0.0006us/node at 0.21% max residual, against 35.54us + 0.0584us/node (1.21%) for the same body doing its node work

The reducer body's per-node cost is 12.94x higher inside the mutative draft than on plain state: body-in-draft per module.reducer call gives 0.7559us/node from 76.54/224.01/401.04/794.69us at 100/500/1000/2000 ops, against 0.0584us/node from 38.93/49.78/64.38/94.19us

Everything create() and the base reducer do around the body stays about 10% of module.reducer wall at every size: 7.90/25.33/43.16/92.68us against 84.43/249.34/444.20/887.37us per call, a share of 9.4/10.2/9.7/10.4%
Timing the reducer does not distort the case: the instrumented replay is 0.983x the untouched Cold miss rebuild (100 operations) and 0.995x at 1000 operations
caveats: The no-cache baseline compares a cold rebuild against a manual replay — both are a replay, so that pair reads about 1x by construction rather than what the cache is worth
The two keyframe cases are floored by a 100ms drain sleep for fire-and-forget keyframe writes to land, so their difference isn't persistence overhead

The body-in-draft leg is not linear in op count: a four-point least-squares fit leaves a 6.29% max residual, against 1.21% on the plain-state leg and 0.21% on the validation leg, so its 0.7559us/node is a secant across 100-2000 ops rather than a rate, and its 33.93us fitted intercept carries that curvature and should not be read against the plain leg's
Input validation is 89.6% of the plain-state reducer body at 100 ops but 37.7% at 2000, so schema construction dominating the body is a statement about the small end of the range

Recorded on a developer laptop with the user's own Firefox, a VM and a DAW resident, which is the standing condition for this series; an earlier attempt at this same record was discarded unrecorded because a second write-cache bench in another worktree overlapped its start and a Spotlight index of a fresh node_modules tree ran throughout, which moved the draft leg's per-node slope to 13.77x and its fit residual to 13.15% against the 12.94x and 6.29% here

title: write-cache microbenchmarks
question: write-cache hit and miss cost against PGlite
conclusions: In Write Cache Cold Miss Performance, Cold miss rebuild (1000 operations) is 17.97x slower than Cold miss with keyframe optimization (100 ops, keyframe at 50)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit with multiple revisions in ring buffer is 1.13x slower than Cache hit (latest revision)
In Write Cache Warm Miss Performance, Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations) is 6.43x slower than Warm miss with nearby cached revision
In Write Cache LRU Eviction Performance, LRU eviction (filling cache to capacity) is 3x slower than LRU access pattern (updating access order)
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline, No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (1000 operations) is 64.56x slower than With cache: rebuild (100 operations)
In Write Cache Keyframe Performance, Keyframe persistence overhead (every 10th revision) is 1.01x slower than Without keyframe persistence (interval = 1000000)
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (100 ops), cold miss 100 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 2.14x slower than cold miss 100 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (500 ops), cold miss 500 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 2.31x slower than cold miss 500 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (1000 ops), cold miss 1000 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 2.51x slower than cold miss 1000 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (2000 ops), cold miss 2000 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay is 2.79x slower than cold miss 2000 ops: input validation only
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Read/Write Split, draft leg 2000 ops: real body (fidelity reference) is 172071.97x slower than plain leg 100 ops: no body: create() + base reducer only
caveats: The no-cache baseline compares a cold rebuild against a manual replay — both are a replay, so that pair reads about 1x by construction rather than what the cache is worth
The two keyframe cases are floored by a 100ms drain sleep for fire-and-forget keyframe writes to land, so their difference isn't persistence overhead

title: write-cache microbenchmarks
question: write-cache hit and miss cost against PGlite
conclusions: In Write Cache Cold Miss Performance at 100 operations, Cold miss rebuild (100 operations) is 1.33x slower than Cold miss with keyframe optimization (100 ops, keyframe at 50)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit with multiple revisions in ring buffer is 1.11x slower than Cache hit (latest revision)

In Write Cache Warm Miss Performance, no two cases ran the same stated operation count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: Warm miss rebuild (10 incremental operations) at 801.38 ops/sec, Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations) at 407.09 ops/sec, Warm miss with nearby cached revision at 1168.77 ops/sec
In Write Cache LRU Eviction Performance, LRU eviction (filling cache to capacity) is 2.97x slower than LRU access pattern (updating access order)
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline at 100 operations, With cache: rebuild (100 operations) is 1.57x slower than No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (100 operations)

title: auth-scope microbenchmarks
question: auth evaluation cost per step, isolated from storage
conclusions: In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) at 100 grants, evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), match first is 1.02x slower than evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), denied

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > group principals, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: 10 grants, group of 10 members at 3488941.75 ops/sec, 10 grants, group of 1000 members at 106047.01 ops/sec, 10 grants, group absent from the map at 6035145.96 ops/sec

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > conditions, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: evaluateCondition: single comparison at 12750469.91 ops/sec, evaluateCondition: 100 nodes, depth 2 at 480452.87 ops/sec, evaluateCondition: max depth 10 at 495361.91 ops/sec, evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants x 100 condition nodes at 4915.4 ops/sec, evaluateGrantStack: 100 conditional grants, no context at 7891170.66 ops/sec

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation at 10 grants, retention: 10 grants, shadow walk before an anyone allow is 26.71x slower than retention: 10 grants, administered from the top

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation at 100 grants, retention: 100 grants, shadow walk before an anyone allow is 112.93x slower than retention: 100 grants, administered from the bottom
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L4_AUTH_CONDITIONS: 100 grants is 6.67x slower than L0_CLEAN: 100 grants

In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead) > group fan-out at L3, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: 1 distinct group(s) at 586359.01 ops/sec, 2 distinct group(s) at 413592.82 ops/sec, 5 distinct group(s) at 210689.25 ops/sec
In read gate (scopePredicate) at 100 grants, ModelReadGate: 100 grants is 1.03x slower than ModelReadGate: 100 grants, denied subject

In read gate (scopePredicate) > group roster serving, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: 1 referencer(s), reader outside the audience at 280948.85 ops/sec, 10 referencer(s), reader outside the audience at 44727.02 ops/sec, 100 referencer(s), reader outside the audience at 4821.61 ops/sec

title: write-cache microbenchmarks
question: write-cache hit and miss cost against PGlite
conclusions: In Write Cache Cold Miss Performance at 100 operations, Cold miss rebuild (100 operations) is 1.34x slower than Cold miss with keyframe optimization (100 ops, keyframe at 50)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit (exact revision match) runs at 0.97x the rate of Cache hit (latest revision)
In Write Cache Hit Performance, Cache hit (exact revision match) runs at 1.11x the rate of Cache hit with multiple revisions in ring buffer

In Write Cache Warm Miss Performance, no two cases ran the same stated operation count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: Warm miss rebuild (10 incremental operations) at 811.3 ops/sec, Warm miss rebuild (50 incremental operations) at 413.45 ops/sec, Warm miss with nearby cached revision at 1186.91 ops/sec

In Write Cache LRU Eviction Performance, LRU eviction (filling cache to capacity) over 12 documents, capacity 6 is 1.05x slower than LRU access pattern (updating access order) over 12 documents, capacity 12
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline at 100 operations, With cache: rebuild (100 operations) is 1.59x slower than No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (100 operations)
In Write Cache vs No-Cache Baseline at 1000 operations, With cache: rebuild (1000 operations) is 1.02x slower than No-cache baseline: manual rebuild (1000 operations)
In Write Cache Keyframe Performance, Keyframe persistence overhead (every 10th revision) is 1.01x slower than Without keyframe persistence (interval = 1000000)
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (100 ops), cold miss 100 ops: input validation only runs at 28.45x the rate of cold miss 100 ops: reducer body on plain state
In Write Cache Cold Miss Replay Decomposition (100 ops), cold miss 100 ops: reducer body on plain state runs at 11.73x the rate of cold miss 100 ops: instrumented cold-miss replay

title: auth-scope microbenchmarks
question: auth evaluation cost per step, isolated from storage
conclusions: In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) at 100 grants, evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), match first runs at 1.04x the rate of evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), match last
In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) at 100 grants, evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), match last runs at 0.97x the rate of evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants (cap), denied

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > group principals, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: 10 grants, group of 10 members at 3502263.2 ops/sec, 10 grants, group of 1000 members at 105443.98 ops/sec, 10 grants, group absent from the map at 5938572.8 ops/sec

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > conditions, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: evaluateCondition: single comparison at 12799685.89 ops/sec, evaluateCondition: 100 nodes, depth 2 at 479355.96 ops/sec, evaluateCondition: max depth 10 at 493433.3 ops/sec, evaluateGrantStack: 100 grants x 100 condition nodes at 4923.29 ops/sec, evaluateGrantStack: 100 conditional grants, no context at 7717175.35 ops/sec

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation at 10 grants, retention: 10 grants, administered from the top runs at 2.77x the rate of retention: 10 grants, administered from the bottom

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation at 10 grants, retention: 10 grants, administered from the top runs at 24.62x the rate of retention: 10 grants, shadow walk before an anyone allow

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation at 100 grants, retention: 100 grants, administered from the top runs at 0.62x the rate of retention: 100 grants, administered from the bottom

In auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) > auth scope write validation at 100 grants, retention: 100 grants, administered from the top runs at 67.79x the rate of retention: 100 grants, shadow walk before an anyone allow
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L0_CLEAN: 100 grants runs at 1.01x the rate of L0_POLICIED: 100 grants
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L0_POLICIED: 100 grants runs at 0.99x the rate of L1_DOCUMENT_DECISIONS: 100 grants
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L1_DOCUMENT_DECISIONS: 100 grants runs at 5.66x the rate of L2_AUTH_ENFORCEMENT: 100 grants
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L2_AUTH_ENFORCEMENT: 100 grants runs at 1.16x the rate of L3_AUTH_GROUPS: 100 grants
In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead), L3_AUTH_GROUPS: 100 grants runs at 1.01x the rate of L4_AUTH_CONDITIONS: 100 grants

In admission gate vs no-gate baseline (decideAtHead) > group fan-out at L3, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: 1 distinct group(s) at 594519.54 ops/sec, 2 distinct group(s) at 404235.44 ops/sec, 5 distinct group(s) at 212681.12 ops/sec
In read gate (scopePredicate) at 100 grants, ModelReadGate: 100 grants is 1x slower than ModelReadGate: 100 grants, denied subject

In read gate (scopePredicate) > group roster serving, no two cases ran the same stated grant count, member count, node count, referencer count or group count, so the suite has no spread that isolates the mechanism: 1 referencer(s), reader outside the audience at 275798.67 ops/sec, 10 referencer(s), reader outside the audience at 44672.6 ops/sec, 100 referencer(s), reader outside the audience at 4836.76 ops/sec
caveats: auth policy evaluation (pure CPU) / evaluateGrantStack: 2 grants: rme 6.86%, so the run measured noise as much as the system
